text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's former Prime Minister Andrei Lukanov, a deputy of the ruling Socialists, was shot dead at his home around 9:10 local time on Wednesday.
In a nationwide address President Zhelyu Zhelev urged "decisisve and uncompomising measures ... against all acts of terrorism", describing the murder as a political one.

-- Bulgarians' foreign currency deposits in an insolvent bank should be blocked for six months after the court declares the bank insolvent under a draft amendment to the deposit guarantee law, proposed by the parliament's budget committee chairman.
Now Bulgarians can draw their foreign currency deposits in banks that expect a court ruling on their insolvency in four equal tranches over two years.

-- Member countries of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) gave unanimous clearance for the admission of Bulgaria to the trade body. Bulgaria's parliament was expected to ratify the entry by December 6, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's current deep economic crisis pushes the country further away from NATO, Bulgaria's Defence Minister Dimitar Pavlov said after talks with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana in Brussels.
-- The World Bank planned to extend an additional loan to Bulgaria to support its central heating system running this winter, a bank spokesman said.

-- A recently adopted scheme for setting Bulgaria's energy prices monthly in line with the lev/dollar exchange rate are illegal because they infringe principles of market competition and the cabinet should cancel them, the country's Competition Protection Commission said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to decide by October 30 whether it will sign a barter deal for the import of 16 TU-204 and TU-234 Russian-made passenger aircraft, Transport Ministry officials said.

-- Bulgaria now is very close to an agreement with the International Monetary Fund for the release of a delayed second $115 million tranche, Bulgaria's central bank governer Lyubomir Filipov said in Washington.
-- We will not let this terrorist act (ex-prime minister Anrei Lukanov's murder) lead to a state of emergency in Bulgaria, the parliament said in a statement.
-- The railroad link from Sofia to the border with Serbia will be completely electrified by December 1, the Bulgarian State Railway director general said.
